Conjecture Some functional of the Wedderburn-weighted Hoefsmit character data at q_0 carries nuclear shell structure. The Wedderburn-weighted nuclear character signal \delta^2\Phi(Z), computed purely from the substrate parameter q_0 (per-partition Hoefsmit characters at Hecke levels k = 3\ldots 10, with no empirical input), is conjectured to carry nuclear shell structure.

For each partition \lambda \vdash k with Wedderburn weight w_\lambda = \dim_q(\lambda)^2/[k]_q!, the nuclear braid \mathcal{N}(Z, Z) has character \chi_\lambda(Z) computed from the Hoefsmit seminormal matrices. The cumulative Wedderburn-weighted signal

  \Phi(Z) = \sum_{k=3}^{K} \sum_{\lambda \vdash k} w_\lambda \, \ln|\chi_\lambda(Z)|

has forward second difference \delta^2 \Phi(Z) = \Phi(Z) - 2\Phi(Z{-}1) + \Phi(Z{-}2), which at K = 10 and q_0 takes the values

Z \delta^2 \Phi (K{=}10) Magic?
8 +33.25 \star
20 +20.40 \star
28 +4.43 \star

These three values are reproducible from q_0 with no empirical input. What they do not establish is any relation between \delta^2\Phi and the magic numbers; see the scope below.

Scope — this is a conjecture, and the tabulated values above are not evidence for it. Three measured facts bound what the signal can support. Each was obtained by re-running the producer over the full range Z \le 32, not by inspecting the three magic Z alone.

1. The sign of \delta^2\Phi is a parity test. Over Z = 3 \ldots 31 at K = 10, \delta^2\Phi(Z) > 0 holds precisely when Z is even, with no exceptions. Every magic number is even, so the positivity property is satisfied by every even Z and distinguishes none of them.

2. The magic numbers are not maxima. Among even Z at K = 10 the local maxima are Z \in \{4, 12, 16\} — none magic — and the global maximum is Z = 12. The magic Z = 8 ranks sixth of the fourteen even Z in range, below the non-magic Z = 10 and Z = 12. The earlier reading of the table above as showing elevation at the magic numbers came from tabulating only magic Z; the non-magic contrast reverses it.

3. No value of q repairs this. Sweeping q across 1 < q < \varphi (49 points, K = 8) moves the peak monotonically downward through Z — the global maximum runs 12 \to 16 \to 14 \to 12 \to 10 \to 8 as q rises — so the signal is genuinely q-dependent. But Z = 20 and Z = 2 are local maxima at no sampled q, and the best overlap with the magic set anywhere in the interval is two of four maxima. The parity property itself holds only for q \lesssim 1.16 and fails above.

What survives is the construction and its q-dependence, not the identification. Whether some other functional of the same Hoefsmit data carries shell structure is open; the second difference of the Wedderburn-weighted log-character, at any q in the interval tested, does not. The selection principle remains open at Proposition (homological shell condensation): BB-stratified E_\infty^{p,>0}(n) = 0 at magic n.

This threading link interpolates between the parent and daughter nuclear configurations.

Setup.

In beta decay \mathcal{N}(Z, N) \to \mathcal{N}(p\!+\!1, n\!-\!1), a neutron \mathfrak{n} = [\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{d}]_p becomes a proton \mathfrak{p} = [\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}]_p. The threading link L_0.

The smoothing L_0 resolves the crossing between the converting quark strand and the surrounding nuclear link. Its topology depends on the local linking structure around the converting nucleon.

For a nucleus where the converting neutron sits inside a closed sub-link (shell closure), L_0 threads through that closed sub-link. The threading link's Alexander polynomial encodes the shell structure:

The parent \mathcal{N}(6, 8) has a magic neutron number n = 8. The 8 neutrons form a closed sub-link (the p-shell closure). The converting neutron sits inside this closure. The smoothing L_0 threads through the remaining 7 nucleons of the closed sub-link and the 6 protons of the core.

Level 1: Internal (Borromean).

The crossing change \mathfrak{d} \to \mathfrak{u} inside \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{d}) is a Skein resolution at the d-d crossing of the Borromean link. This represents the intrinsic Borromean suppression. The Borromean link resists the internal crossing change by a factor of [1]_q [2]_q / [3]_q.

The resulting L_0 = \mathcal{L}_H embeds in the multi-nucleon link \mathcal{N}(Z, N). It threads through Z protons and n - 1 remaining neutrons. The threading modulates the Markov trace by a factor depending on the shell structure of the nuclear environment:

  • Closed shell. When n or p sits at a magic number, the inter-nucleon crossings form a chain of non-commuting TL generators adjacent to L_0. The Markov trace picks up a factor f(m, k, q) depending on the chain length m and the position k of the converting nucleon within the shell.

prop:sdp-regime-switch:
Proposition Discrete regime switches in SDP cross-channel couplings across isotopes. The semidefinite-programming (SDP) extension of the LP-dual operator-selection framework (BW coefficient shadow price) introduces matrix-valued cross-block couplings c_{\lambda\lambda'}. These couple conjugate-partition pairs in the Wedderburn decomposition of H_n(q). At fixed substrate parameter q_0, these couplings vary discretely with (Z, N). Isolated zeros mark nuclear-structure regime switches (shell closures, pairing transitions, and jet-level crossings).

At each (Z, N), the atom braid word W_{\mathrm{atom}} has a YSN character \chi_\lambda(W) in every irrep \lambda. These characters serve as primal observables driving the SDP:

  \Phi_{\lambda\lambda} \;=\; \frac{|\chi_\lambda(W)|^2}{\lVert W \rVert^2}

The SDP dual has a 2 \times 2 PSD block per conjugate pair (\lambda, \lambda'):

  \begin{pmatrix}
    \mu_\lambda - y_0 - y_\lambda & c_{\lambda\lambda'} \\
    c_{\lambda\lambda'} & \mu_{\lambda'} - y_0 - y_{\lambda'}
  \end{pmatrix}
  \;\succeq\; 0

Here, \mu_\lambda is the q-Laplacian eigenvalue and c_{\lambda\lambda'} is the coupling determined by the atom observables.

A regime switch occurs at (Z, N) values where c_{\lambda\lambda'} \to 0. The PSD block drops from rank 2 to rank 1, the active-constraint set of the SDP jumps, and the atom's density matrix loses coherence between \lambda and \lambda'.

\square

The SDP is solved numerically, with a scalar-LP fallback.

sec:strangelet-intro:
In the lepton-partner reading of the quark sector (knot–particle dictionary), the strange quark's partner T_{2,5}^\sigma carries five crossings whereas the down quark's partner T_{2,3}^\sigma carries three; the quarks themselves are unknot strands of \mathcal{B}_3. Inside the cores of massive neutron stars, degenerate Fermi pressure overcomes this skein-energy threshold and drives a three-stage topological phase transition:

Stage 1 — Borromean dissolution (\rho \gtrsim 2\rho_0): Under extreme baryon chemical potential, the three-strand Borromean confinement links \mathcal{B}_3 (whose hyperbolic complement volume \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 8G \approx 7.32772 carries 99\% of the nucleon rest mass) begin to delocalize.

Because the Hopf link complement is Seifert-fibered with \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{L}_H) = 0, the transition from Borromean baryons (749 skein units) to Hopf diquarks (3 skein units)—a factor of 250 in binding scale—drops the effective carrier mass while stiffening the equation of state toward the conformal sound-speed limit c_s^2 = 1/3.

prop:crossing-energy-decomposition:
Proposition Crossing energy decomposes into strong and Coulomb channels. The crossing energy assigns +q to positive crossings and -q^{-1} to negative crossings (q > 1). Writing q = e^\lambda with \lambda = \ln q > 0, the weights decompose into symmetric and antisymmetric components under the mirror operation \sigma:

  q = \cosh\lambda + \sinh\lambda, \qquad
  q^{-1} = \cosh\lambda - \sinh\lambda.

Equivalently, in the form that exhibits the mirror action, reversing a crossing negates its \cosh part and leaves its \sinh part unchanged:

  +q = +\cosh\lambda + \sinh\lambda, \qquad -q^{-1} = -\cosh\lambda + \sinh\lambda.

Statement. Let \mathfrak{H} be a knot composite carrying p positive and m negative crossings, so that \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}) = pq - mq^{-1}.

  1. Channel decomposition. Summing the two weights above over the composite gives

      E_{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathfrak{H}) = (p - m)\cosh\lambda,
  \qquad
  E_{\mathrm{asym}}(\mathfrak{H}) = (p + m)\sinh\lambda,

    and these reconstruct the crossing energy exactly: \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}) = E_{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathfrak{H}) + E_{\mathrm{asym}}(\mathfrak{H}). The two channels carry different multiplicities, p - m against p + m, because the \sinh part is blind to the crossing sign.

  2. Mirror behaviour. The mirror \sigma reverses every crossing, exchanging p and m. Hence

      E_{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathfrak{H}^{\sigma}) = -E_{\mathrm{sym}}(\mathfrak{H}),
  \qquad
  E_{\mathrm{asym}}(\mathfrak{H}^{\sigma}) = E_{\mathrm{asym}}(\mathfrak{H}).

    The symmetric total negates and the antisymmetric total is fixed. This inverts the parity of the weight functions themselves, where \cosh is even and \sinh is odd in \lambda, because under \sigma the multiplicity flips as well.

  3. Pair cancellation. For a particle-antiparticle pair (\mathfrak{H}, \mathfrak{H}^{\sigma}) the symmetric contributions cancel and the antisymmetric contributions add:

      \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}) + \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}^{\sigma})
  = 2E_{\mathrm{asym}}(\mathfrak{H}).

  4. Ratio identity. For a positive braid closure, that is m = 0 with p \geq 1, the antisymmetric-to-symmetric ratio is

      \frac{E_{\mathrm{asym}}}{E_{\mathrm{sym}}}
  = \tanh(\ln q),

    independent of the crossing number p. For a composite with mixed crossing signs and p \neq m the ratio acquires the multiplicity factor

      \frac{E_{\mathrm{asym}}}{E_{\mathrm{sym}}}
  = \frac{p + m}{p - m}\,\tanh(\ln q),

    so it is not independent of \mathfrak{H} in general.
prop:strangelet-crossing-energy:
Proposition Crossing energy of strange quark matter is purely strong. Let \mathcal{S}_N be a composite of N baryon-number units of strange quark matter. Each unit contains one up, one down, and one strange quark in a Borromean triple \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{s}) linked by the Hopf link \mathcal{L}_H. Explicitly:

1. Electromagnetic neutrality. The Coulomb charge (Coulomb charge) of each baryon-number unit vanishes:

  Q(\mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{s}))
  =  +\tfrac{2}{3} - \tfrac{1}{3} - \tfrac{1}{3}
  =  0.

The strangelet is electromagnetically neutral for all q > 0. The vanishing depends only on the crossing orientation partition within the Borromean structure, evaluated on the canonical n = 3 word. It is an invariant of that canonical presentation, not a topological invariant of the closure: Q is writhe-derived, and the writhe shifts by \pm 1 under stabilisation. Fixing the minimal level is what makes the statement well-posed, and the Borromean word is already at its braid index.

2. Purely antisymmetric crossing energy. With Q = 0 the symmetric channel vanishes and the crossing energy reduces to:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathcal{S}_N)
  =
  N \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}(n_+ + n_-)(q - q^{-1}).

The entire crossing energy lies in the antisymmetric channel (decomposition): the symmetric multiplicity is the writhe n_+ - n_-, which is what Q = 0 annihilates, while the antisymmetric multiplicity is the crossing count n_+ + n_-, which Q = 0 leaves untouched.

Open. Under this assignment the strangelet has zero symmetric content and maximal antisymmetric content, which is the opposite of the physical reading in items 1 and 3. Whether "electromagnetic neutrality" survives, and whether the enhanced-binding argument below still follows, requires re-deriving those items rather than relabelling them — the identification of the antisymmetric channel with electromagnetism is itself not established.

Separately: the Q values used in item 1 are not representable. The Coulomb charge is \tfrac{1}{2}(n_+ - n_-) \in \tfrac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z}, so +\tfrac{2}{3} and -\tfrac{1}{3} are outside its range for every braid word. Item 1 computes Q from assigned quark charges rather than from crossing counts, so the two are distinct quantities sharing a symbol. The vanishing of the sum is unaffected, but it is not a statement about the crossing-count Q that item 2 uses.

3. Enhanced binding per baryon. The strange quark \mathfrak{s} \leftarrow T_{2,5}^{\sigma} contributes 5 negative crossings to the Borromean braid word, versus 3 for the down quark \mathfrak{d} \leftarrow T_{2,3}^{\sigma}. For each baryon unit:

The arrow is the knot-particle dictionary's lepton-descent relation, not an identity: that table gives the quark's braid element in \mathcal{B}_3 as a single generator, \sigma_i for \mathfrak{u} and \sigma_i^{-1} for \mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{s} — consistent with the up quark being "the unknot distinguished by its environment". The crossing counts 5 and 3 are read off the descent partner and are unaffected.

  n_-^{(\mathrm{uds})} = 3 + 5 = 8,
  \qquad
  n_-^{(\mathrm{udd})} = 3 + 3 = 6.

The binding component per baryon satisfies:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}^{(\mathrm{uds})}
  =  8q^{-1}
   >  6q^{-1}
  =  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}^{(\mathrm{udd})}.

Strange matter has strictly more strong binding per baryon than neutron matter for all q > 0.

The down and strange quarks occupy tubes with negative orientation (-1/3 each). The Coulomb charge Q = \frac{1}{2}(n_+ - n_-) vanishes by the partition \{+, -, -\}, independent of knot type.

(2) This is immediate from \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}} = \text{strong} + Q \cdot (q - q^{-1}) with Q = 0.

(3) The crossing count follows from the braid index. The trefoil T_{2,3} has minimal braid word \sigma_1^3 (3 crossings). The cinquefoil T_{2,5} has \sigma_1^5 (5 crossings). rem:strangelet-witten-stability:

The strangelet crossing energy provides a translation of Witten's hypothesis.

Crossing-energy argument. The strangelet proposition yields three facts.

  1. SQM is electromagnetically neutral (Q = 0).
  2. Its crossing energy is purely strong.
  3. Its strong binding per baryon exceeds neutron matter by a factor of 4/3.

Replacing down quarks (lepton partner T_{2,3}^{\sigma}, 3 negative crossings) with strange quarks (lepton partner T_{2,5}^{\sigma}, 5 negative crossings) grants each baryon 2q^{-1} additional strong binding. At q = q_0, this gives 1.802 Skein units per baryon.

At q_{\mathrm{gold}} = 1/\varphi^2 \approx 0.382, the elliptic fiber degenerates. \mathcal{E}_q acquires a node. Two roots of the Weierstrass equation coincide. The three color tubes collapse to a degenerate configuration. At this point:

  1. The S_5 symmetry that enforces color neutrality breaks.
  2. The q-chromaticity gamut expands to fill the entire triangle.
  3. Individual quarks acquire positive probability. They are no longer confined.

This is deconfinement. It is a topological phase transition where the fiber that enforces confinement ceases to exist.

First-order character. The QGP transition in QCD lattice simulations is first-order for three or more light quark flavors. In QOU, the first-order character is visible algebraically.

  1. Discriminant crossing. The discriminant of \mathcal{E}_q crosses zero at q_{\mathrm{gold}}. For q > q_{\mathrm{gold}}, \Delta < 0 (smooth curve, one real component). At q = q_{\mathrm{gold}}, \Delta = 0 (nodal curve). Below, \Delta > 0 (two real components, then degenerate). The topology of the real locus changes discontinuously.
  2. Latent heat. The energy difference between the confined phase and the deconfined phase is finite. In crossing-energy units, the latent heat per baryon is
  \mathcal{L}
   \sim 
  \tfrac{1}{2}(n_+ + n_-)\bigl[(q + q^{-1}) -
  (q_{\mathrm{gold}} + q_{\mathrm{gold}}^{-1})\bigr]

This is nonzero for q \neq q_{\mathrm{gold}}. 3. Order parameter. The order parameter is the j-invariant of the elliptic fiber. j(q) is finite and continuous for q > q_{\mathrm{gold}}. It diverges as q \to q_{\mathrm{gold}} (j \to \infty at the node). The divergence of j signals the breakdown of the elliptic structure. The Polyakov loop jumps from zero (confined) to nonzero (deconfined) at the transition.

Effective q at finite temperature. The physical substrate has q = q_0. Temperature changes the effective crossing energy available to disrupt the Borromean structure. At temperature T, thermal fluctuations supply energy \sim k_B T per degree of freedom. Deconfinement occurs when thermal energy matches the Hopf binding energy per baryon:

  k_B T_c
   \sim 
  |\mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{p})|
   \sim 
  \tfrac{1}{2}(q + q^{-1}) \cdot n_{\mathrm{link}},

where n_{\mathrm{link}} is the number of Hopf-link crossings in the Borromean triple. The effective q at which the chiral structure of the fiber is thermally disrupted is q_{\mathrm{gold}}.

This identifies the QGP transition temperature with the stability margin:

  \frac{k_B T_c}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}}
   \sim 
  \frac{q - q_{\mathrm{gold}}}{q}
  = 
  \frac{q_0 - 0.382}{q_0}
   \approx  0.656.

Golden ratio threshold. The QGP phase transition is not at a new scale or coupling constant. It is the same golden ratio that appears in the chiral degeneration, the Penrose tiling, and the E_8 McKay correspondence. Its appearance as the deconfinement boundary is forced by the S_5 symmetry of Bring's surface. The minimal polynomial s^2 + s - 1 = 0 governs both the chiral fiber structure and the confinement mechanism. When the fiber degenerates, confinement breaks.

def:hopf-diquark:
Definition Hopf diquark. A Hopf diquark is a pair of quarks (\mathfrak{q}_i^a, \mathfrak{q}_j^b) in distinct color tubes a \neq b of Bring's surface, joined by the Hopf link \mathcal{L}_H:

  D_{ij}^{[ab]}
  = 
  \mathfrak{q}_i^a  \oplus  \mathfrak{q}_j^b,

where i, j \in \{\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{s}\} denote flavor indices and a, b \in \{r, g, b\} denote color indices. The bracket [ab] denotes antisymmetry: D_{ij}^{[ab]} = -D_{ij}^{[ba]}.
rem:hopf-diquark-remark:
Remark Color antitriplet and the sign of Hopf linking. Color representation. The two quarks each carry a color index. Their antisymmetric combination [ab] transforms in the color antitriplet \bar{\mathbf{3}}_c of \mathrm{SU}(3):

  \bar{\mathbf{3}}_c
  = 
  \epsilon^{abc}\mathfrak{q}^b \otimes \mathfrak{q}^c.

The antisymmetry D^{[ab]} = -D^{[ba]} arises from Hopf linking. The linking number is \mathrm{lk}(a, b) = +1 while \mathrm{lk}(b, a) = -1 under component exchange.
